meta.title: Romanian A2 Elementary
meta.subtitle: 750 more words, none of them in A1 · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Romanian → English (see the Romanian, recall the meaning) and English → Romanian (see an English meaning, recall the Romanian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 750 words for an elementary learner, aligned to A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance' — a learner here is able to manage simple, routine exchanges of information on familiar matters — personal and family information, shopping, the local area, work — and to describe in simple terms their background, their surroundings and what they immediately need. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be — no openly licensed graded word list for Romanian was found to build it from. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 455 of the 750 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — relatives and the people around you, jobs and study, clothes, more food and cooking, the rooms and furniture of a home, the town and its services, travel and holidays, nature, the seasons and the compass, animals, health and the body, feelings and character, free time and sport, the parts of the day and telling what happened when, the higher numbers, and the everyday verbs of moving, dressing, cooking and doing — and the other 295 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Romanian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword carries its pronunciation in the International Phonetic Alphabet, Wiktionary's own, because Romanian does not write where the stress falls. Verbs are given in the dictionary's form, with the infinitive's a (a face, to do). The 445 nouns show their gender — masculine, feminine or neuter, the neuter being masculine in the singular and feminine in the plural — their plural, and their definite form, the article being a suffix (casă, a house; casa, the house); the 154 verbs show their first person, past participle and subjunctive, and behind the All forms fold their present, imperfect, subjunctive and imperative by person. Real example sentences come with 736 of the 750 words, three apiece for 684 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, gender, forms and pronunciation: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
